headline: Adani Group plans $120 billion capex, wins major power supply contract
summary: Adani Group outlines a massive $120 billion 5-6 year capex plan, while subsidiary AESL secures a major 1,750 MW renewable energy contract in West Bengal. Adani Airports raises $300 million to expand non-aero infrastructure, and CRISIL upgrades Adani Power's credit rating to AA+.

stories.what: Adani Group plans to invest over $120 billion over the next 5-6 years across infrastructure, energy, and data centres. Reported by Business Standard via a Jefferies research note, the group aims to keep its net debt below 3.5 times EBITDA during this expansion.
stories.why: Demonstrates the group's aggressive expansion strategy across core verticals while maintaining leverage discipline.
stories.watch: Execution timelines for data centres under AdaniConneX
stories.title: Adani Group planning $120 bn in capex over next 5-6 years: Jefferies

stories.what: Powerpulse Trading Solutions, a subsidiary of Adani Energy Solutions Limited, received a Letter of Award from WBSEDCL to supply 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable energy for 25 years starting July 1, 2028. The contract includes a 750 MW greenshoe option.
stories.why: Secures long-term cash flow predictability and expands the group's presence in round-the-clock clean energy contracts.
stories.watch: Whether WBSEDCL exercises the 750 MW greenshoe option
stories.title: AESL arm secures 1,750 MW RE-RTC supply contract from WBSEDCL

stories.what: Adani Airport Holdings signed a binding agreement to raise ₹2,790 crore ($300 million) by selling up to a 1.55% stake to 360 ONE Asset. The funds will be used to develop non-aeronautical commercial infrastructure such as city-side hotels.
stories.why: Drives higher margin, non-regulated commercial revenue growth across airport properties.
stories.watch: Commercial monetization milestones for airport real estate
stories.title: Adani Airports chases fast-growing non-aero revenues with latest $300-mn fund raise

stories.what: CRISIL upgraded Adani Power's credit rating to CRISIL AA+/Stable from CRISIL AA/Stable covering bank loans and NCD facilities worth ₹90,500 crore. The upgrade is attributed to a strong business profile and a high share of power purchase agreements.
stories.why: Lowers borrowing costs and signals improving balance sheet strength for thermal assets.
stories.watch: Impact on future debt refinancing costs
stories.title: CRISIL upgrades Adani Power's rating to AA+/Stable

stories.what: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board directed Adani Green Energy to stop excavation work at its Tarali hydropower project over alleged missing permissions. The company stated the stopped work only involves support facilities, while main components hold statutory clearances.
stories.why: Highlights regulatory and environmental compliance friction risk in execution of hydro assets.
stories.watch: MPCB response to the company's clarification on support facilities
stories.title: Adani’s Tarali project: The dispute over its cost and wildlife fee

stories.what: Adani signed a 3-year copper supply deal with Attero, as reported by Moneycontrol. India currently holds nearly 1.3 million tonnes per year of refining capacity but remains reliant on imports.
stories.why: Secures essential raw material feedstocks for expanding electrical equipment and grid infrastructure businesses.
stories.watch: Ramp up of domestic copper processing volume
stories.title: Adani signs 3-year copper supply deal with Attero: Report

stories.what: Adani Cement announced plans to deploy 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to move clinker and cement, with initial units deployed at its Sanghi plant in Gujarat and full fleet operational by March 2027.
stories.why: Reduces carbon intensity in cement logistics while lowering operational fuel costs.
stories.watch: Target deployment speed ahead of the March 2027 deadline
stories.title: Adani Cement to deploy 410 heavy-duty electric trucks

stories.what: Adani Defence & Aerospace announced that its Bagheera AT1 vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile completed No Cost No Commitment demonstration trials at Pokhran. CEO Ashish Rajvanshi stated the system has 60% indigenous content.
stories.why: Demonstrates progress in building domestic defence manufacturing capabilities under the Make in India framework.
stories.watch: Potential procurement orders from the Indian Armed Forces
stories.title: 'Screwdrivergiri' at work again? Is Adani's Bagheera AT1 vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile a Russian weapon in Indian clothing?

concept.explain: A greenshoe option is a provision in a contract or offer that allows the issuer or seller to expand the transaction size beyond the initial target. In today's power deal, WBSEDCL secured 1,750 MW of power with an option to purchase an extra 750 MW under identical terms. For infrastructure players, it provides a built-in upside to scale revenues without re-bidding.

question.q: Why is Adani Airports raising private equity for non-aeronautical infrastructure instead of core airport operations?
question.a: Aeronautical revenues are heavily regulated based on cost-plus tariffs set by regulators. Non-aeronautical assets like city-side hotels, retail, and duty-free offer unregulated, higher-margin growth, making equity funding attractive for rapid commercial development.

script: Good morning, Aashish. Here is your Adani briefing for Wednesday, 25 November. We start with the overall group strategy. Jefferies reports that the Adani Group is planning a 120 billion dollar capital expenditure plan over the next 5 to 6 years, targeting infrastructure, energy, and data centres. Management aims to keep net debt below 3.5 times EBITDA, balancing aggressive growth with leverage control. Moving to power and utilities, Powerpulse Trading Solutions, a subsidiary of Adani Energy Solutions Limited, secured a major 25-year contract from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Limited. The company will supply 1,750 megawatts of round-the-clock renewable energy starting July 2028. The deal includes a 750 megawatt greenshoe option, which could boost total contracted capacity to 2,500 megawatts. In credit markets, CRISIL upgraded Adani Power Limited's rating to CRISIL AA+/Stable for facility limits worth 90,500 crore rupees. The rating agency cited a strong business profile backed by power purchase agreements. Over at Adani Airports, the company raised 300 million dollars, or 2,790 crore rupees, by selling up to a 1.55 percent stake to 360 ONE Asset. This capital will fund commercial, non-aeronautical developments like city-side hotels to drive recurring income. In environmental compliance, the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board ordered Adani Green Energy Limited to halt excavation at its Tarali hydro project over missing clearances. The company clarified that the work is limited to support structures, while main project components hold all required permits. On the industrial supply side, Moneycontrol reports that the group signed a 3-year copper supply agreement with Attero to support manufacturing needs, as national refining capacity remains constrained. For sustainability efforts, Adani Cement announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks by March 2027 to transport clinker and cement, deploying the initial units at its Sanghi plant in Gujarat. Finally, in defence, Adani Defence and Aerospace completed trials for its Bagheera anti-tank missile at Pokhran. CEO Ashish Rajvanshi stated the system has 60 percent indigenous content. Today's concept to note is the greenshoe option, illustrated by the West Bengal power win. It allows buyers to expand contracted volume on pre-agreed terms without running new tenders. As you head into meetings, think about this question: Why raise equity specifically for airport non-aero infrastructure? The answer lies in regulation. Core airport tariffs are strictly capped, whereas non-aero assets like retail and hotels yield higher, unregulated profit margins.
